question: On 19 January 2024, the Greek government published – via the Special Department for the Just Development Transition and as part of the Fifth Written Procedure of the Assessment Plan for the Just Development Transition Programme 2021-2027 – the four specialisation documents concerning the proposed actions for strengthening new and existing small, medium and large enterprises that are either operating or will operate in priority areas of the territorial just development transition plans in the context of Priority 1 of the Just Development Transition Programme (Strengthening and Promoting Entrepreneurship)1.
Bearing in mind the provisions of the Just Transition Fund Regulation, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does the allocation of 45.4 % (EUR 150 million) of the total funding to large enterprises not go against the spirit of the regulation with regard to prioritising funding for SMEs?

Does the criterion of the minimum allocated budget of EUR 500 000 foreseen in the two specialisation documents dedicated to SMEs not contradict the regulation, considering that this criterion will exclude most local SMEs?
Does the absence of climate neutrality as a criterion for assessing investment plans not go against the spirit of the regulation?
answer: 1. The Just Transition Fund (2) allows productive investments to undertakings ‘other than small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)’ to be supported, provided that, according to the Territorial Just Transition Plan, these investments are necessary to mitigate job losses caused by the green transition, without limiting the amount of resources allocated to support such investments.
The Greek Territorial Just Transition Plans include a gap analysis demonstrating that the expected job losses would exceed the expected number of jobs created in the absence of the investment.

Therefore, the Just Transition Development Programme allocates EUR 150 million (3) to support enterprises other than SMEs to create the necessary ecosystems for offsetting the consequences of the lignite-fired plant withdrawal. 2. The Managing Authority of the programme has decided to launch various calls to categories of very small, small and medium-sized enterprises, all open to local and non-local enterprises.

Regarding the minimum threshold, beyond the call for support to SMEs for investments above EUR 500 000, there are calls for de minimis assistance to very small and small enterprises for investments varying from EUR 30 000 to EUR 100 000. In parallel, local SMEs will also be able to apply for support from the Programme ‘Competitiveness’ and the relevant Regional Programmes. 3.

The Greek Just Transition Fund programme is in line with the provisions of the Just Transition Fund Regulation (4), by contributing fully to the achievements of climate objectives. Whilst the programme objective is to accompany the regions from exiting from lignite production and combustion, the regulation does not contain any requirement for any specific intervention to be climate neutral.
